# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN

Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.

optional group] ```

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1465 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1465 - **Title**: gh-1460 [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1460` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +271 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:17:24Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T05:06:17Z ## PR Description Closes #1460 ### What changed The `fa-tokens:` segment-close line now carries the session's model id: the usage-chain fold captures each segment's **last-seen** model (the model that served its final request) and the pinned line shape grows an optional `"model":""` key after `"segment"`, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable — and priceable — downstream. ### Key decisions - Model is captured **from the chain** (assistant-message `model` field), not the CLI's live config: a resume with a different model attributes each segment to the model that actually served it, and the value stays rebuildable (I6). - Last-seen wins: mid-session fallback take-overs stamp the segment with the model that finished it; zero-filled fallbacks (`unknown`) and blank ids never clobber a seen model. - `UsageSegment.model` is a transient field — **usage.json's schema is untouched**; only the log line changes. - Regex compatibility: `usageTokensLogPattern` grows the optional group `(?:,"model":"[^"]*")?` — legacy lines (no model observed) emit the exact old shape and still parse; the repo's single strict consumer is the pinned constant itself (updated here, AC3). - No writer changes needed: `_flushUsageLedger` already passes the folded segment, so the model rides the existing call. Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```
### Verification status - `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **116/116 pass** (branch merged with latest `origin/main` including the v1.0.541 release chore; the guard suite confirms lockfile sync). - `dart analyze` on the touched files — clean. - Three full-suite attempts (`dart test --exclude-tags browser-ext`) covered the whole tree: the only failures are **13 pre-existing environment ones**, each reproduced **identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree** (verified before/without this change): `headless_log_file_test` ×4, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` ×2, `headless_tools_flag_test` ×2, `backend_mode_cli_test` ×5 (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaks a live provider queue into spawned CLI subprocesses instead of the mock LLM); plus the 4 `browser_ext` e2e fixtures need Chrome (absent here — excluded tag). - The full suite also aborts natively (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`, exit 134) in `test/cli/` around `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` — **reproduced with 0 failures on the pristine base worktree**; a pre-existing runner/VM environment crash, unrelated to this change (validation CI is the safety net).

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1465 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1465 - **Title**: gh-1460 [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1460` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +271 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:17:24Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T05:06:17Z ## PR Description Closes #1460 ### What changed The `fa-tokens:` segment-close line now carries the session's model id: the usage-chain fold captures each segment's **last-seen** model (the model that served its final request) and the pinned line shape grows an optional `"model":""` key after `"segment"`, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable — and priceable — downstream. ### Key decisions - Model is captured **from the chain** (assistant-message `model` field), not the CLI's live config: a resume with a different model attributes each segment to the model that actually served it, and the value stays rebuildable (I6). - Last-seen wins: mid-session fallback take-overs stamp the segment with the model that finished it; zero-filled fallbacks (`unknown`) and blank ids never clobber a seen model. - `UsageSegment.model` is a transient field — **usage.json's schema is untouched**; only the log line changes. - Regex compatibility: `usageTokensLogPattern` grows the optional group `(?:,"model":"[^"]*")?` — legacy lines (no model observed) emit the exact old shape and still parse; the repo's single strict consumer is the pinned constant itself (updated here, AC3). - No writer changes needed: `_flushUsageLedger` already passes the folded segment, so the model rides the existing call. Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```
### Verification status - `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **116/116 pass** (branch merged with latest `origin/main` including the v1.0.541 release chore; the guard suite confirms lockfile sync). - `dart analyze` on the touched files — clean. - Three full-suite attempts (`dart test --exclude-tags browser-ext`) covered the whole tree: the only failures are **13 pre-existing environment ones**, each reproduced **identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree** (verified before/without this change): `headless_log_file_test` ×4, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` ×2, `headless_tools_flag_test` ×2, `backend_mode_cli_test` ×5 (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaks a live provider queue into spawned CLI subprocesses instead of the mock LLM); plus the 4 `browser_ext` e2e fixtures need Chrome (absent here — excluded tag). - The full suite also aborts natively (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`, exit 134) in `test/cli/` around `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` — **reproduced with 0 failures on the pristine base worktree**; a pre-existing runner/VM environment crash, unrelated to this change (validation CI is the safety net).

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1465 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1465 - **Title**: gh-1460 [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1460` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +271 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:17:24Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T05:06:17Z ## PR Description Closes #1460 ### What changed The `fa-tokens:` segment-close line now carries the session's model id: the usage-chain fold captures each segment's **last-seen** model (the model that served its final request) and the pinned line shape grows an optional `"model":""` key after `"segment"`, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable — and priceable — downstream. ### Key decisions - Model is captured **from the chain** (assistant-message `model` field), not the CLI's live config: a resume with a different model attributes each segment to the model that actually served it, and the value stays rebuildable (I6). - Last-seen wins: mid-session fallback take-overs stamp the segment with the model that finished it; zero-filled fallbacks (`unknown`) and blank ids never clobber a seen model. - `UsageSegment.model` is a transient field — **usage.json's schema is untouched**; only the log line changes. - Regex compatibility: `usageTokensLogPattern` grows the optional group `(?:,"model":"[^"]*")?` — legacy lines (no model observed) emit the exact old shape and still parse; the repo's single strict consumer is the pinned constant itself (updated here, AC3). - No writer changes needed: `_flushUsageLedger` already passes the folded segment, so the model rides the existing call. Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```
### Verification status - `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **116/116 pass** (branch merged with latest `origin/main` including the v1.0.541 release chore; the guard suite confirms lockfile sync). - `dart analyze` on the touched files — clean. - Three full-suite attempts (`dart test --exclude-tags browser-ext`) covered the whole tree: the only failures are **13 pre-existing environment ones**, each reproduced **identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree** (verified before/without this change): `headless_log_file_test` ×4, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` ×2, `headless_tools_flag_test` ×2, `backend_mode_cli_test` ×5 (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaks a live provider queue into spawned CLI subprocesses instead of the mock LLM); plus the 4 `browser_ext` e2e fixtures need Chrome (absent here — excluded tag). - The full suite also aborts natively (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`, exit 134) in `test/cli/` around `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` — **reproduced with 0 failures on the pristine base worktree**; a pre-existing runner/VM environment crash, unrelated to this change (validation CI is the safety net).

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

Usage:
  dmtools list                           # List available MCP tools
  dmtools doctor                         # Check current directory configuration
  dmtools run <json-file>                # Execute job with JSON config file
  dmtools run <job-name> [--key value]   # Execute a registered job without a config file
  dmtools run <json-file> <encoded>      # Execute job with file + encoded overrides
  dmtools <tool> [args...]              # Execute MCP tool with args
  dmtools <tool> --data '{"json"}'      # Execute with inline JSON
  dmtools <tool> --file params.json     # Execute with JSON file
  dmtools <tool> --verbose              # Execute with verbose output
  dmtools <tool> --debug                # Execute with debug output and error messages
  dmtools <tool> <<EOF                  # Execute with heredoc
  {"json": "data"}
  EOF

Examples:
  dmtools list
  dmtools doctor
  dmtools run job-config.json
  dmtools run codegenerator --param1 test
  dmtools jira_get_ticket DMC-479 summary,description
  dmtools jira_get_ticket --data '{"key": "DMC-479", "fields": ["summary"]}'

Environment Variables:
  DMTOOLS_INTEGRATIONS    Comma-separated list of integrations (jira,confluence,figma)

Environment Files:
  The tool automatically loads environment variables from dmtools.env
  (project root first, then the current working directory).

  Common variables:
  - JIRA_BASE_PATH, JIRA_EMAIL, JIRA_API_TOKEN
  - CONFLUENCE_BASE_PATH, CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN
  - FIGMA_API_KEY
  - GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY
  - SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, BITBUCKET_TOKEN

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1465 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1465 - **Title**: gh-1460 [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1460` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +271 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:17:24Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T05:06:17Z ## PR Description Closes #1460 ### What changed The `fa-tokens:` segment-close line now carries the session's model id: the usage-chain fold captures each segment's **last-seen** model (the model that served its final request) and the pinned line shape grows an optional `"model":""` key after `"segment"`, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable — and priceable — downstream. ### Key decisions - Model is captured **from the chain** (assistant-message `model` field), not the CLI's live config: a resume with a different model attributes each segment to the model that actually served it, and the value stays rebuildable (I6). - Last-seen wins: mid-session fallback take-overs stamp the segment with the model that finished it; zero-filled fallbacks (`unknown`) and blank ids never clobber a seen model. - `UsageSegment.model` is a transient field — **usage.json's schema is untouched**; only the log line changes. - Regex compatibility: `usageTokensLogPattern` grows the optional group `(?:,"model":"[^"]*")?` — legacy lines (no model observed) emit the exact old shape and still parse; the repo's single strict consumer is the pinned constant itself (updated here, AC3). - No writer changes needed: `_flushUsageLedger` already passes the folded segment, so the model rides the existing call. Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```
### Verification status - `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **116/116 pass** (branch merged with latest `origin/main` including the v1.0.541 release chore; the guard suite confirms lockfile sync). - `dart analyze` on the touched files — clean. - Three full-suite attempts (`dart test --exclude-tags browser-ext`) covered the whole tree: the only failures are **13 pre-existing environment ones**, each reproduced **identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree** (verified before/without this change): `headless_log_file_test` ×4, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` ×2, `headless_tools_flag_test` ×2, `backend_mode_cli_test` ×5 (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaks a live provider queue into spawned CLI subprocesses instead of the mock LLM); plus the 4 `browser_ext` e2e fixtures need Chrome (absent here — excluded tag). - The full suite also aborts natively (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`, exit 134) in `test/cli/` around `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` — **reproduced with 0 failures on the pristine base worktree**; a pre-existing runner/VM environment crash, unrelated to this change (validation CI is the safety net).

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1465 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1465 - **Title**: gh-1460 [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1460` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +271 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:17:24Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T05:06:17Z ## PR Description Closes #1460 ### What changed The `fa-tokens:` segment-close line now carries the session's model id: the usage-chain fold captures each segment's **last-seen** model (the model that served its final request) and the pinned line shape grows an optional `"model":""` key after `"segment"`, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable — and priceable — downstream. ### Key decisions - Model is captured **from the chain** (assistant-message `model` field), not the CLI's live config: a resume with a different model attributes each segment to the model that actually served it, and the value stays rebuildable (I6). - Last-seen wins: mid-session fallback take-overs stamp the segment with the model that finished it; zero-filled fallbacks (`unknown`) and blank ids never clobber a seen model. - `UsageSegment.model` is a transient field — **usage.json's schema is untouched**; only the log line changes. - Regex compatibility: `usageTokensLogPattern` grows the optional group `(?:,"model":"[^"]*")?` — legacy lines (no model observed) emit the exact old shape and still parse; the repo's single strict consumer is the pinned constant itself (updated here, AC3). - No writer changes needed: `_flushUsageLedger` already passes the folded segment, so the model rides the existing call. Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```
### Verification status - `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **116/116 pass** (branch merged with latest `origin/main` including the v1.0.541 release chore; the guard suite confirms lockfile sync). - `dart analyze` on the touched files — clean. - Three full-suite attempts (`dart test --exclude-tags browser-ext`) covered the whole tree: the only failures are **13 pre-existing environment ones**, each reproduced **identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree** (verified before/without this change): `headless_log_file_test` ×4, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` ×2, `headless_tools_flag_test` ×2, `backend_mode_cli_test` ×5 (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaks a live provider queue into spawned CLI subprocesses instead of the mock LLM); plus the 4 `browser_ext` e2e fixtures need Chrome (absent here — excluded tag). - The full suite also aborts natively (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`, exit 134) in `test/cli/` around `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` — **reproduced with 0 failures on the pristine base worktree**; a pre-existing runner/VM environment crash, unrelated to this change (validation CI is the safety net).

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1465 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1465 - **Title**: gh-1460 [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1460` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +271 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:17:24Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T05:06:17Z ## PR Description Closes #1460 ### What changed The `fa-tokens:` segment-close line now carries the session's model id: the usage-chain fold captures each segment's **last-seen** model (the model that served its final request) and the pinned line shape grows an optional `"model":""` key after `"segment"`, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable — and priceable — downstream. ### Key decisions - Model is captured **from the chain** (assistant-message `model` field), not the CLI's live config: a resume with a different model attributes each segment to the model that actually served it, and the value stays rebuildable (I6). - Last-seen wins: mid-session fallback take-overs stamp the segment with the model that finished it; zero-filled fallbacks (`unknown`) and blank ids never clobber a seen model. - `UsageSegment.model` is a transient field — **usage.json's schema is untouched**; only the log line changes. - Regex compatibility: `usageTokensLogPattern` grows the optional group `(?:,"model":"[^"]*")?` — legacy lines (no model observed) emit the exact old shape and still parse; the repo's single strict consumer is the pinned constant itself (updated here, AC3). - No writer changes needed: `_flushUsageLedger` already passes the folded segment, so the model rides the existing call. Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```
### Verification status - `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **116/116 pass** (branch merged with latest `origin/main` including the v1.0.541 release chore; the guard suite confirms lockfile sync). - `dart analyze` on the touched files — clean. - Three full-suite attempts (`dart test --exclude-tags browser-ext`) covered the whole tree: the only failures are **13 pre-existing environment ones**, each reproduced **identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree** (verified before/without this change): `headless_log_file_test` ×4, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` ×2, `headless_tools_flag_test` ×2, `backend_mode_cli_test` ×5 (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaks a live provider queue into spawned CLI subprocesses instead of the mock LLM); plus the 4 `browser_ext` e2e fixtures need Chrome (absent here — excluded tag). - The full suite also aborts natively (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`, exit 134) in `test/cli/` around `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` — **reproduced with 0 failures on the pristine base worktree**; a pre-existing runner/VM environment crash, unrelated to this change (validation CI is the safety net).

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1465 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1465 - **Title**: gh-1460 [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1460` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 8 - **Additions**: +271 - **Deletions**: -19 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T23:17:24Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-11T05:06:17Z ## PR Description Closes #1460 ### What changed The `fa-tokens:` segment-close line now carries the session's model id: the usage-chain fold captures each segment's **last-seen** model (the model that served its final request) and the pinned line shape grows an optional `"model":""` key after `"segment"`, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable — and priceable — downstream. ### Key decisions - Model is captured **from the chain** (assistant-message `model` field), not the CLI's live config: a resume with a different model attributes each segment to the model that actually served it, and the value stays rebuildable (I6). - Last-seen wins: mid-session fallback take-overs stamp the segment with the model that finished it; zero-filled fallbacks (`unknown`) and blank ids never clobber a seen model. - `UsageSegment.model` is a transient field — **usage.json's schema is untouched**; only the log line changes. - Regex compatibility: `usageTokensLogPattern` grows the optional group `(?:,"model":"[^"]*")?` — legacy lines (no model observed) emit the exact old shape and still parse; the repo's single strict consumer is the pinned constant itself (updated here, AC3). - No writer changes needed: `_flushUsageLedger` already passes the folded segment, so the model rides the existing call. Version files stay at 1.0.541 in sync with the merged main release (root + flutter_app + lockfile; the nightly desktop-leg guard suite passes). ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart ``` End-to-end: a headless run logs `fa-tokens: {"sessionId":…,"segment":0,"model":"test-model","input":…}` matching the pinned regex.
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR CHAIN[Session JSONL chain] --> SCAN[UsageChainScanner] SCAN -->|last-seen model| SEG[UsageChainSegment.model] SEG --> FOLD[UsageFolder.foldSegment] FOLD --> US[UsageSegment.model
transient, not in usage.json] US --> LINE[usageTokensLogLine] LINE -->|optional key| OUT["fa-tokens: {…,"model":"id",…}"] OUT --> REGEX[usageTokensLogPattern
optional group] ```
### Verification status - `dart test test/nightly_desktop_leg_guard_test.dart test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **116/116 pass** (branch merged with latest `origin/main` including the v1.0.541 release chore; the guard suite confirms lockfile sync). - `dart analyze` on the touched files — clean. - Three full-suite attempts (`dart test --exclude-tags browser-ext`) covered the whole tree: the only failures are **13 pre-existing environment ones**, each reproduced **identically on a pristine `origin/main` worktree** (verified before/without this change): `headless_log_file_test` ×4, `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` ×2, `headless_tools_flag_test` ×2, `backend_mode_cli_test` ×5 (the runner's ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` leaks a live provider queue into spawned CLI subprocesses instead of the mock LLM); plus the 4 `browser_ext` e2e fixtures need Chrome (absent here — excluded tag). - The full suite also aborts natively (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned fastbin chunk detected`, exit 134) in `test/cli/` around `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` — **reproduced with 0 failures on the pristine base worktree**; a pre-existing runner/VM environment crash, unrelated to this change (validation CI is the safety net).

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

# gh-1460: [GOAL] fa-tokens ledger: add model id to the segment-close line (priceable factory token rows)

## Description

## Goal

The `fa-tokens:` ledger line (gh-1241 surface 2) must carry the session's model id, so every token row the factory publishes is attributable to a model — and therefore priceable.

## Subject

`lib/src/usage/usage_log_line.dart` (pinned shape, AC7) + the writer in the segment-close path (`usage_chain.dart` / `agent_cli.dart`). Current pinned shape: `{"sessionId","segment","input","output","cacheRead","requests","source"}` — no model.

## Capability surface

- New optional field `"model":"<provider/model-id>"` — the id fa already knows for the session's provider (the same string settings/UI display).
- Backward/forward compatibility: the pinned regex grows an OPTIONAL group (`("model":"…")?`), old consumers keep parsing old lines; new lines parse in old consumers that use tolerant JSON (the factory summarizer is JSON-based — fine; strict-regex consumers must be updated in the same PR).
- Placement: emit once per segment-close line, last-seen model wins downstream (awf summarizer already captures it — awf 233263e).
- Docs: gh-1241 shape table + the pinned regex constant updated together.

## Acceptance criteria

1. AC1: a session on a named model emits `fa-tokens:` lines containing `"model":"<id>"`; the regex in `usage_log_line.dart` matches.
2. AC2: a legacy line without `model` still parses (old fixtures green).
3. AC3: strict consumers updated in the same PR (grep the repo for the pinned regex).
4. AC4: unit tests: new-shape parse, old-shape parse, model passthrough to the usage chain.

## Test plan

- L1: unit tests (new/old shapes, model capture).
- L2: replay a recorded session output through the summarizer — model lands in the row.
- L3 (live): one factory leg publishes a row with a non-empty model on the board data branch.

## Non-goals

- Pricing computation (dmtools-agents card).
- Multi-model-per-segment attribution (last-seen wins; per-request attribution is a separate ask).

## References

- Downstream: awf 233263e (summarizer model passthrough, deployed), dmtools-agents board pricing card (cross-ref).
- Original pin: gh-1241.

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0239549Z # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0240493Z # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0241382Z # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0242221Z # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0242912Z dart_blocker=""
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0243538Z # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0244390Z # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245156Z # through with zero gates executed.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245969Z [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0246898Z # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0247987Z # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0248779Z # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0249431Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0250385Z   [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251315Z fi
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251757Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0252655Z   [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0253535Z fi
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0254067Z # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0254892Z #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0255749Z #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0256564Z #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0257384Z #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0258602Z #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0259401Z #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0260232Z #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0261101Z #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0261930Z #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0262882Z #     hostage (the v1.0.519-521 starvation).

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0239549Z # Verdict pass collects blockers WITHOUT exiting, so dart_ok is
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0240493Z # always exported explicitly ('true' or 'false', never '') —
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0241382Z # publish and the Provider smoke read this output and an empty
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0242221Z # value must never read as either (review thread on #1370).
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0242912Z dart_blocker=""
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0243538Z # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0244390Z # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245156Z # through with zero gates executed.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245969Z [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0246898Z # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0247987Z # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0248779Z # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0249431Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0250385Z   [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251315Z fi
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251757Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0252655Z   [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0253535Z fi
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0254067Z # #1368 — two independent verdicts over the needs legs:
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0254892Z #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0255749Z #     gate dart_ok AND the aggregate — analyze/test/coverage must
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0256564Z #     gate the publish (review thread: the case bodies were
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0257384Z #     swapped in the first cut, re-enshrining the starvation);
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0258602Z #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0259401Z #     fa-aot-build, installer-verify, install-pin-gate,
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0260232Z #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0261101Z #     only: they redden the required aggregate but NEVER dart_ok —
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0261930Z #     a red Windows build must not hold the pure-Dart publish

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0242912Z dart_blocker=""
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0243538Z # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0244390Z # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245156Z # through with zero gates executed.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245969Z [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0246898Z # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0247987Z # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0248779Z # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0249431Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0250385Z   [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251315Z fi
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251757Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0252655Z   [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0253535Z fi

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0254892Z #   PACKAGE legs (everything NOT platform) → dart_blocker: they

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0258602Z #   PLATFORM/NATIVE/PTY legs (build-web/android/ios/macos,

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0260232Z #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:

    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0244390Z # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245156Z # through with zero gates executed.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0245969Z [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || dart_blocker="changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0246898Z # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0247987Z # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0248779Z # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0249431Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251315Z fi
2026-10-11T04:57:43.0251757Z if [ -z "$dart_blocker" ]; then

2026-10-11T04:57:43.0260232Z #     cube-kernel-live, cli-visual-settings, pty-*) → platform_red

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
  # `model_request_summary` records and the session chain's record shape —
  # a shape change there breaks the fold even when every regular leg is
  # green, so this suite is a merge gate for trajectory/session/usage
  # diffs. Gate model (2026-09 dispatch-only CI): this workflow has NO
  # pull_request trigger — the SM dispatches it on the PR head, so
  # `github.event_name` is never 'pull_request' and a PR-only `if` would
  # leave this leg permanently skipped (REG-1 gating nothing). On real PR
  # events the path classifier narrows it to usage-relevant diffs; on every
  # other event (main/tags/schedule/release + SM validation dispatches)
  # the full gate runs, so the suite runs there too. Same latent bug still
  # pending for perf-gate (issue #303) — flagged in the gh-1243 rework.
  usage-fold:
    name: Usage fold (ledger chain)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      needs.changes.outputs.usagefold == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Usage-fold suite
        # The path classifier also gates on ^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$
        # — the CLI wiring test that exercises that file must run here too,
        # otherwise a wiring regression merges behind a green test/usage.
        run: dart test test/usage test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart
