# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on

  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block

  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a

  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue

  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml

    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

blocks.text:
Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
  # `model_request_summary` records and the session chain's record shape —

  # the full gate runs, so the suite runs there too. Same latent bug still

  usage-fold:
    name: Usage fold (ledger chain)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

blocks.text:
Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. Also consider increasing runs (median of 5 → 7) for robustness. But keep runtime bounded — the whole file currently takes seconds; 250k costs ~25ms per test pair, trivial.

Wait — but does raising base actually help? Jitter is proportional-ish: a scheduling pause of ~5ms hits an 8ms measurement as hard as it hits a 3ms one. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

But careful about "true ratio" — with min statistics, small could be measured on the fastest possible cache state and doubled on... min over enough runs converges to the true compute time. A genuinely quadratic implementation would still show ~4x ratio with mins. That's the robust fix.

However, changing median→min changes the helper used by the absolute-budget tests too. I could keep median for absolute budgets (they have generous headroom: post-fix median 33ms vs 100ms budget) and use min-of-N for the growth-shape ratios. Or simpler: increase runs for growth tests.

Let me combine conservatively, minimal diff:
- `medianWrapMs` add a `statistic` option? Keep it simple: for the growth tests, run each size more times (e.g., 9) and take the median — a pause inflating the median of 9 requires ≥5 of 9 samples inflated, much less likely. And raise base to 200k for ASCII so the window is ~7ms.

Total added runtime: growth tests: 3 tests × 2 sizes × (1 warm + 9 runs) ≈ 3×2×10 wraps of 200-800k cells ≈ 3×2×10×~10-40ms ≈ ~3s. Currently they're at 100k/200k with 5 runs ≈ 3×2×6×~3-7ms ≈ <1s. Fine for a perf test file.

Hmm, but honestly the cleanest, most defensible fix targeting the exact failure mode: use min-of-N for growth ratio (noise robust), keep median for absolute budgets (headroom). Min-of-9: for quadratic regression, min still shows ~4x. Let me verify that claim locally: the file says "the old quadratic candidates (re-scan per emitted row) measure ~4x+". Min-of-N would preserve that. Yes.

Actually, is there a risk that min-of-9 makes the test too lenient in catching small superlinear factors (e.g., n log n ~2.2x)? threshold 3.2 still gates those. OK.

Let me also double-check: is there an existing pattern in the repo for this (gh-1357)? Let me search for gh-1357 to follow precedent.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.

# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:

    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA

    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by

    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI

Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. Also consider increasing runs (median of 5 → 7) for robustness. But keep runtime bounded — the whole file currently takes seconds; 250k costs ~25ms per test pair, trivial.

Wait — but does raising base actually help? Jitter is proportional-ish: a scheduling pause of ~5ms hits an 8ms measurement as hard as it hits a 3ms one. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

But careful about "true ratio" — with min statistics, small could be measured on the fastest possible cache state and doubled on... min over enough runs converges to the true compute time. A genuinely quadratic implementation would still show ~4x ratio with mins. That's the robust fix.

However, changing median→min changes the helper used by the absolute-budget tests too. I could keep median for absolute budgets (they have generous headroom: post-fix median 33ms vs 100ms budget) and use min-of-N for the growth-shape ratios. Or simpler: increase runs for growth tests.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI

Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. Also consider increasing runs (median of 5 → 7) for robustness. But keep runtime bounded — the whole file currently takes seconds; 250k costs ~25ms per test pair, trivial.

Wait — but does raising base actually help? Jitter is proportional-ish: a scheduling pause of ~5ms hits an 8ms measurement as hard as it hits a 3ms one. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

But careful about "true ratio" — with min statistics, small could be measured on the fastest possible cache state and doubled on... min over enough runs converges to the true compute time. A genuinely quadratic implementation would still show ~4x ratio with mins. That's the robust fix.

However, changing median→min changes the helper used by the absolute-budget tests too. I could keep median for absolute budgets (they have generous headroom: post-fix median 33ms vs 100ms budget) and use min-of-N for the growth-shape ratios. Or simpler: increase runs for growth tests.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

What's the right fix for rework? The failing test is a perf-threshold test that flaked on a loaded CI runner (3.65 vs 3.2; other legs of the same test passed: CJK 2x<=3.2 passed, hard-cut passed). Options:

1. Re-run CI (no code change) — but the rework pack requires a code fix; also after 3 reds on the same head, validation waits for a NEW head. So pushing a new commit is required anyway.

2. Look at the test — maybe it's inherently flaky and the repo has a mechanism for perf test retries or quarantine (there's a "Flake quarantine list guard"). Check how similar flakes are handled. Maybe bump iterations/median or widen threshold. But careful: the test was recently added in #1502 (perf work). Changing the threshold could be considered gaming.

Let me look at the test first.

Root cause identified: CI shard 0/4 failed on `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — a timing flake (ratio 3.65 vs 3.2 threshold) from the freshly merged main perf change (#1502), unrelated to this PR's usage code. Let me examine the test.
{"path":"/home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness/test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart"}

The flake: at 100k/200k cells, times are tiny (3.31ms / 12.09ms) — at these small sizes, timer jitter dominates: ratio of 3.65 when the true asymptotic ratio is ~2x. The CJK and single-word variants passed. The ASCII prose path is the fastest (batched), so at 100k cells the measurement is only ~3.3ms — noise floor.

Fix options:
1. Increase base size for ASCII prose (e.g., 200k/400k) so measurements are well above the noise floor. Times were 3.31ms and 12.09ms — 12ms for doubled... wait if linear, doubling 100k→200k should be ~2x. 3.31→12.09 is 3.65x. Hmm, but the 1M test passes <100ms, so 100k should be ~10ms if linear... it measured 3.31ms at 100k and the 1M measured under 100ms — 1M/100k=10x → if linear, 1M ≈ 33ms, well under 100. So why 12.09ms for 200k? 200k should be ~6.6ms linear. 12.09 is nearly 2x that... hmm, maybe cache effects. Anyway, median of 5 runs still jittered.
