# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
  # `model_request_summary` records and the session chain's record shape —
  # a shape change there breaks the fold even when every regular leg is
  # green, so this suite is a merge gate for trajectory/session/usage
  # diffs. Gate model (2026-09 dispatch-only CI): this workflow has NO
  # pull_request trigger — the SM dispatches it on the PR head, so
  # `github.event_name` is never 'pull_request' and a PR-only `if` would
  # leave this leg permanently skipped (REG-1 gating nothing). On real PR
  # events the path classifier narrows it to usage-relevant diffs; on every
  # other event (main/tags/schedule/release + SM validation dispatches)
  # the full gate runs, so the suite runs there too. Same latent bug still
  # pending for perf-gate (issue #303) — flagged in the gh-1243 rework.
  usage-fold:
    name: Usage fold (ledger chain)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      needs.changes.outputs.usagefold == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Usage-fold suite
        # The path classifier also gates on ^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$
        # — the CLI wiring test that exercises that file must run here too,
        # otherwise a wiring regression merges behind a green test/usage.
        run: dart test test/usage test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart

Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. Also consider increasing runs (median of 5 → 7) for robustness. But keep runtime bounded — the whole file currently takes seconds; 250k costs ~25ms per test pair, trivial.

Wait — but does raising base actually help? Jitter is proportional-ish: a scheduling pause of ~5ms hits an 8ms measurement as hard as it hits a 3ms one. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

But careful about "true ratio" — with min statistics, small could be measured on the fastest possible cache state and doubled on... min over enough runs converges to the true compute time. A genuinely quadratic implementation would still show ~4x ratio with mins. That's the robust fix.

However, changing median→min changes the helper used by the absolute-budget tests too. I could keep median for absolute budgets (they have generous headroom: post-fix median 33ms vs 100ms budget) and use min-of-N for the growth-shape ratios. Or simpler: increase runs for growth tests.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
  # `model_request_summary` records and the session chain's record shape —
  # a shape change there breaks the fold even when every regular leg is
  # green, so this suite is a merge gate for trajectory/session/usage
  # diffs. Gate model (2026-09 dispatch-only CI): this workflow has NO
  # pull_request trigger — the SM dispatches it on the PR head, so
  # `github.event_name` is never 'pull_request' and a PR-only `if` would
  # leave this leg permanently skipped (REG-1 gating nothing). On real PR
  # events the path classifier narrows it to usage-relevant diffs; on every
  # other event (main/tags/schedule/release + SM validation dispatches)
  # the full gate runs, so the suite runs there too. Same latent bug still
  # pending for perf-gate (issue #303) — flagged in the gh-1243 rework.
  usage-fold:
    name: Usage fold (ledger chain)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      needs.changes.outputs.usagefold == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Usage-fold suite
        # The path classifier also gates on ^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$
        # — the CLI wiring test that exercises that file must run here too,
        # otherwise a wiring regression merges behind a green test/usage.
        run: dart test test/usage test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart

blocks.text:
Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. Also consider increasing runs (median of 5 → 7) for robustness. But keep runtime bounded — the whole file currently takes seconds; 250k costs ~25ms per test pair, trivial.

Wait — but does raising base actually help? Jitter is proportional-ish: a scheduling pause of ~5ms hits an 8ms measurement as hard as it hits a 3ms one. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

But careful about "true ratio" — with min statistics, small could be measured on the fastest possible cache state and doubled on... min over enough runs converges to the true compute time. A genuinely quadratic implementation would still show ~4x ratio with mins. That's the robust fix.

However, changing median→min changes the helper used by the absolute-budget tests too. I could keep median for absolute budgets (they have generous headroom: post-fix median 33ms vs 100ms budget) and use min-of-N for the growth-shape ratios. Or simpler: increase runs for growth tests.

Let me combine conservatively, minimal diff:
- `medianWrapMs` add a `statistic` option? Keep it simple: for the growth tests, run each size more times (e.g., 9) and take the median — a pause inflating the median of 9 requires ≥5 of 9 samples inflated, much less likely. And raise base to 200k for ASCII so the window is ~7ms.

Total added runtime: growth tests: 3 tests × 2 sizes × (1 warm + 9 runs) ≈ 3×2×10 wraps of 200-800k cells ≈ 3×2×10×~10-40ms ≈ ~3s. Currently they're at 100k/200k with 5 runs ≈ 3×2×6×~3-7ms ≈ <1s. Fine for a perf test file.

Hmm, but honestly the cleanest, most defensible fix targeting the exact failure mode: use min-of-N for growth ratio (noise robust), keep median for absolute budgets (headroom). Min-of-9: for quadratic regression, min still shows ~4x. Let me verify that claim locally: the file says "the old quadratic candidates (re-scan per emitted row) measure ~4x+". Min-of-N would preserve that. Yes.

Actually, is there a risk that min-of-9 makes the test too lenient in catching small superlinear factors (e.g., n log n ~2.2x)? threshold 3.2 still gates those. OK.

Let me also double-check: is there an existing pattern in the repo for this (gh-1357)? Let me search for gh-1357 to follow precedent.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same
  # perf-tagged tests for trajectory-touching PRs and aggregates into
  # Quality gate below. `--tags perf` is precise: the only perf-tagged test
  # is the #262 gate (test/integration/trajectory/perf_open_gate_test.dart,
  # lands with #300), so the 97 MB fixture never runs for other PRs.
  perf-gate:
    name: Perf gate (trajectory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.perf == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: dart test --tags perf
        run: dart test --tags perf

  # gh-1241 REG-1: the usage fold consumes the trajectory ledger's
  # `model_request_summary` records and the session chain's record shape —
  # a shape change there breaks the fold even when every regular leg is
  # green, so this suite is a merge gate for trajectory/session/usage
  # diffs. Gate model (2026-09 dispatch-only CI): this workflow has NO
  # pull_request trigger — the SM dispatches it on the PR head, so
  # `github.event_name` is never 'pull_request' and a PR-only `if` would
  # leave this leg permanently skipped (REG-1 gating nothing). On real PR
  # events the path classifier narrows it to usage-relevant diffs; on every
  # other event (main/tags/schedule/release + SM validation dispatches)
  # the full gate runs, so the suite runs there too. Same latent bug still
  # pending for perf-gate (issue #303) — flagged in the gh-1243 rework.
  usage-fold:
    name: Usage fold (ledger chain)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: changes
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      needs.changes.outputs.usagefold == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Usage-fold suite
        # The path classifier also gates on ^lib/src/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger\.dart$
        # — the CLI wiring test that exercises that file must run here too,
        # otherwise a wiring regression merges behind a green test/usage.
        run: dart test test/usage test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart

Options for the fix:
1. **Fix the test's noise sensitivity** (raise base cells so the median is above the jitter floor). This is the actual root cause: at 100k cells the ASCII-batched path measures ~3.3ms — timer/scheduling noise on a loaded shared CI runner easily skews a 5-run median at that scale. Raising to e.g. 250k cells (≈8ms base) keeps total runtime similar and is the gh-1357-rule-compliant fix ("a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate").

If true behavior were linear ~3.3→6.6ms, 12.09 is way off — hmm, that suggests something more than jitter? But the same test passed CJK (which is slower per cell) and the 1M ASCII budget test passed in <100ms — meaning 1M ≈ ≤100ms vs 200k at 12ms — 5x size for ≤8x time is consistent-ish with linear + overhead. If 200k took 12.09 while 100k took 3.31, that IS suspicious of superlinearity... unless the 100k median was lucky-fast (JIT/branch/caches) or the 200k unlucky-slow. Given CJK passed (CJK at 100k does ~2x work per cell vs ASCII so times are larger, less noise-sensitive), and hard-cut passed, and the absolute 1M test passed — the batching is linear. blocks.text:
Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. Also consider increasing runs (median of 5 → 7) for robustness. But keep runtime bounded — the whole file currently takes seconds; 250k costs ~25ms per test pair, trivial.

Wait — but does raising base actually help? Jitter is proportional-ish: a scheduling pause of ~5ms hits an 8ms measurement as hard as it hits a 3ms one. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

But careful about "true ratio" — with min statistics, small could be measured on the fastest possible cache state and doubled on... min over enough runs converges to the true compute time. A genuinely quadratic implementation would still show ~4x ratio with mins. That's the robust fix.

However, changing median→min changes the helper used by the absolute-budget tests too. I could keep median for absolute budgets (they have generous headroom: post-fix median 33ms vs 100ms budget) and use min-of-N for the growth-shape ratios. Or simpler: increase runs for growth tests.

Let me combine conservatively, minimal diff:
- `medianWrapMs` add a `statistic` option? Keep it simple: for the growth tests, run each size more times (e.g., 9) and take the median — a pause inflating the median of 9 requires ≥5 of 9 samples inflated, much less likely. And raise base to 200k for ASCII so the window is ~7ms.

Total added runtime: growth tests: 3 tests × 2 sizes × (1 warm + 9 runs) ≈ 3×2×10 wraps of 200-800k cells ≈ 3×2×10×~10-40ms ≈ ~3s. Currently they're at 100k/200k with 5 runs ≈ 3×2×6×~3-7ms ≈ <1s. Fine for a perf test file.

Hmm, but honestly the cleanest, most defensible fix targeting the exact failure mode: use min-of-N for growth ratio (noise robust), keep median for absolute budgets (headroom). Min-of-9: for quadratic regression, min still shows ~4x. Let me verify that claim locally: the file says "the old quadratic candidates (re-scan per emitted row) measure ~4x+". Min-of-N would preserve that. Yes.

Actually, is there a risk that min-of-9 makes the test too lenient in catching small superlinear factors (e.g., n log n ~2.2x)? threshold 3.2 still gates those. OK.

Let me also double-check: is there an existing pattern in the repo for this (gh-1357)? Let me search for gh-1357 to follow precedent.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

arguments.content:
# Rework: gh-1460 (PR #1465) — validation-CI flake fix

## Issues/Notes

- **Validation CI went red on head `32c2d3cf`** (run [38112524699](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38112524699)). Of the four red checks listed in `ci_failures.md`, three are kicker artifacts of the red head — the `Quality gate` / `JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)` / `Binaries smoke gate` check runs in kicker run `38111774140` completed in **under one second with no runner and no steps** (pure re-request fallout, no logs exist). The single real failure was **Core tests (shard 0/4)** (job `114390922043`).
- **Root cause** (from the shard log): `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart: wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time` measured `small=3.31ms / doubled=12.09ms` → ratio **3.65 vs the 3.2 bound**. The doubled-size **median of 5** caught a scheduling pause on the loaded shared runner — the wrap itself is linear: every other leg in the same file passed, including the 1M-cell absolute budget (`< 100ms`) and both other growth legs. This file arrived via the `main` merge (#1502, gh-1496 perf work), not this PR's usage changes.
- **Review threads**: both open threads are an `APPROVE` (no blocking/important issues; one optional note that the gh-1241 shape table lives in the GitHub issue and can only be updated after release) and a machine verdict record marked "Do not edit or reply". Neither carries a `threadId`/`rootCommentId` (top-level comments, not inline threads), so no threaded replies are posted — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.
- **Not changed on purpose**: the absolute-budget legs keep the median statistic — their gh-1357 headroom (~3x between the ~33ms median and the 100ms bound) already prices in the jitter observed on this runner class; only the noise-dominated ~3–7ms growth windows needed the fix.

## Approach

- **RED**: added a deterministic regression test (`growth ratio is pause-proof`) that reproduces the exact CI failure shape with synthetic sample sets — the old median statistic trips at 3.55x, the new min statistic passes at ~2.06x, and a genuinely quadratic pair still trips the min-based ratio at ~4.0x (real superlinear work inflates both sizes, so the minimum cannot hide it).
- **GREEN**: `expectLinearGrowth` now measures with `minWrapMs` — the **minimum over 9 runs** (one warm-up + 9 timed wraps per size) instead of the median of 5. Runner jitter only ever *inflates* a wall-clock sample, so the minimum converges on the true compute time and a pause can no longer tip the doubling ratio; the 3.2 bound and its superlinear-regression catching power are unchanged. The shared timing loop was extracted into `_wrapTimes`; `medianWrapMs` is retained for the two absolute-budget tests.
- Stress verification: the updated file passed **3 consecutive runs on a quiet machine and 3 consecutive runs under full 4-core saturation** (all growth legs green every time; only the median-based absolute-budget legs can trip under that artificial 4x oversubscription, which is far beyond hosted-runner steal time and is exactly the margin gh-1357 headroom covers).
- Pushed as a **new head** `3ce761193` (owner directive: after 3 reds on one head, validation waits for a new head). The kicker's re-requested contexts will re-run against it.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — new `minWrapMs` (min-of-9) statistic + shared `_wrapTimes`; `expectLinearGrowth` switches median→min; new pause-proof regression test; doc comments record the CI run and the rationale.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `## Unreleased` entry documenting the flake fix.

## Test Coverage

- `dart test test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — **7/7 pass** (quiet ×4, under 4-core load ×3).
- `dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **106/106 pass** (the PR's own suites, untouched by this rework).
- `dart test test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` — 9/9 pass.
- `dart analyze test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full-tree suite note (carried from the PR description, unchanged by this rework): 13 pre-existing environment failures reproduced identically on pristine `origin/main` (`FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` ambient leak, absent Chrome) plus a pre-existing native abort in `test/cli/` — validation CI on the new head is the safety net.

Even with 4 load generators saturating all cores, medians stayed healthy. CI's failure had small=3.31ms (fast!) and doubled=12.09ms — i.e., the DOUBLED measurement got the jitter, not the small one. Median of 5 at 200k took 12ms when quiet machines take ~6.7-7ms. That means jitter can inflate a single median by ~1.8x. To trip 3.2 from a baseline ~2.0 you need ~1.6x inflation — plausible on a noisy shared runner (GitHub ubuntu runners are known to be very jittery, with steal time).

I can't easily reproduce the exact flake on this quiet machine, but the mechanism is clear and the fix is well-grounded: the gh-1357 rule stated in the file itself says bounds need "generous headroom over local medians (CI runners jitter; a bound the fix sits at is noise, not a gate)". The growth tests sit at 100k cells where the ASCII-batched path runs ~3.3ms — with a median of only 5 samples, a noisy-neighbor pause lands squarely in the median when the whole measurement window is that short. The CI failure shows exactly this: small=3.31ms was fine but doubled=12.09ms inflated ~1.8x.

The fix: raise the growth-test base size so the timed window is well above the noise floor. E.g., base 250k → small ~8-9ms, doubled ~17-18ms. Also consider increasing runs (median of 5 → 7) for robustness. But keep runtime bounded — the whole file currently takes seconds; 250k costs ~25ms per test pair, trivial.

Wait — but does raising base actually help? Jitter is proportional-ish: a scheduling pause of ~5ms hits an 8ms measurement as hard as it hits a 3ms one. The real robustness lever is the median of more runs plus a longer window. Alternative approach used commonly: measure more runs and take median, or repeat the growth measurement a few times and take the best/minimum ratio (min is robust against inflation jitter since jitter only ever inflates).

Actually a cleaner standard technique for perf gates on noisy CI: take the MINIMUM across runs (min is the statistic robust to positive-only noise like scheduling pauses). Median of 5 can still catch a pause in the middle. Min-of-7 makes inflation flake practically impossible while still catching true superlinearity (which inflates BOTH measurements proportionally — true superlinear work is not noise; ratio of mins still ~4x for quadratic).

But careful about "true ratio" — with min statistics, small could be measured on the fastest possible cache state and doubled on... min over enough runs converges to the true compute time. A genuinely quadratic implementation would still show ~4x ratio with mins. That's the robust fix.

However, changing median→min changes the helper used by the absolute-budget tests too. I could keep median for absolute budgets (they have generous headroom: post-fix median 33ms vs 100ms budget) and use min-of-N for the growth-shape ratios. Or simpler: increase runs for growth tests.

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + one-shot note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist
  steering text after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on
  call+result). gh-1449: the drop note never costs the model a turn — it
  rides the payload's LAST existing user message as an extra text block
  (degenerate no-user-message payload degrades to the legacy standalone
  note), names tool/id/cut/kept-in-summary, and fires ONCE per orphan:
  `orphanReportKey` (canonical id + tool + timestamp) latches in
  `Agent.reportedOrphanKeys`; hosts persist each first-time batch as the
  hidden `orphan_report` custom record and seed the latch back at resume
  (CLI `_loadSession`, app `loadSession`).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail; its report carries `notedOrphanKeys` — the wire frame is
  optional-field backward-compatible); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run
  position-counter ids session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s
  `_localTrimFallback` routes the kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction evictio…

{"content":"# Rework: gh-1460 (PR #1465) — validation-CI flake fix

## Issues/Notes

- **Validation CI went red on head `32c2d3cf`** (run [38112524699](https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38112524699)). Of the four red checks listed in `ci_failures.md`, three are kicker artifacts of the red head — the `Quality gate` / `JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)` / `Binaries smoke gate` check runs in kicker run `38111774140` completed in **under one second with no runner and no steps** (pure re-request fallout, no logs exist). The single real failure was **Core tests (shard 0/4)** (job `114390922043`).
- **Root cause** (from the shard log): `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart: wrap time grows linearly: ASCII prose, 2x input <= 3.2x time` measured `small=3.31ms / doubled=12.09ms` → ratio **3.65 vs the 3.2 bound**. The doubled-size **median of 5** caught a scheduling pause on the loaded shared runner — the wrap itself is linear: every other leg in the same file passed, including the 1M-cell absolute budget (`< 100ms`) and both other growth legs. This file arrived via the `main` merge (#1502, gh-1496 perf work), not this PR's usage changes.
- **Review threads**: both open threads are an `APPROVE` (no blocking/important issues; one optional note that the gh-1241 shape table lives in the GitHub issue and can only be updated after release) and a machine verdict record marked "Do not edit or reply". Neither carries a `threadId`/`rootCommentId` (top-level comments, not inline threads), so no threaded replies are posted — see `outputs/review_replies.json`.
- **Not changed on purpose**: the absolute-budget legs keep the median statistic — their gh-1357 headroom (~3x between the ~33ms median and the 100ms bound) already prices in the jitter observed on this runner class; only the noise-dominated ~3–7ms growth windows needed the fix.

## Approach

- **RED**: added a deterministic regression test (`growth ratio is pause-proof`) that reproduces the exact CI failure shape with synthetic sample sets — the old median statistic trips at 3.55x, the new min statistic passes at ~2.06x, and a genuinely quadratic pair still trips the min-based ratio at ~4.0x (real superlinear work inflates both sizes, so the minimum cannot hide it).
- **GREEN**: `expectLinearGrowth` now measures with `minWrapMs` — the **minimum over 9 runs** (one warm-up + 9 timed wraps per size) instead of the median of 5. Runner jitter only ever *inflates* a wall-clock sample, so the minimum converges on the true compute time and a pause can no longer tip the doubling ratio; the 3.2 bound and its superlinear-regression catching power are unchanged. The shared timing loop was extracted into `_wrapTimes`; `medianWrapMs` is retained for the two absolute-budget tests.
- Stress verification: the updated file passed **3 consecutive runs on a quiet machine and 3 consecutive runs under full 4-core saturation** (all growth legs green every time; only the median-based absolute-budget legs can trip under that artificial 4x oversubscription, which is far beyond hosted-runner steal time and is exactly the margin gh-1357 headroom covers).
- Pushed as a **new head** `3ce761193` (owner directive: after 3 reds on one head, validation waits for a new head). The kicker's re-requested contexts will re-run against it.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — new `minWrapMs` (min-of-9) statistic + shared `_wrapTimes`; `expectLinearGrowth` switches median→min; new pause-proof regression test; doc comments record the CI run and the rationale.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `## Unreleased` entry documenting the flake fix.

## Test Coverage

- `dart test test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — **7/7 pass** (quiet ×4, under 4-core load ×3).
- `dart test test/usage/ test/cli/agent_cli_usage_ledger_test.dart test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart` — **106/106 pass** (the PR's own suites, untouched by this rework).
- `dart test test/changelog_cap_guard_test.dart` — 9/9 pass.
- `dart analyze test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` — clean; `dart format` applied.
- Full-tree suite note (carried from the PR description, unchanged by this rework): 13 pre-existing environment failures reproduced identically on pristine `origin/main` (`FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` ambient leak, absent Chrome) plus a pre-existing native abort in `test/cli/` — validation CI on the new head is the safety net.
